Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating this young male patient in your clinic. He was born at term following an uncomplicated gestation and delivery. The family history is negative for early childhood medical conditions, and his mother took standard prenatal vitamins consistently.

On physical examination, he appears well-nourished and rests comfortably in no acute distress. His respiratory examination reveals clear breath sounds bilaterally without tachypnea or retractions. Femoral and radial pulses are symmetric and easily palpable throughout, and abdominal examination reveals soft, non-tender quadrants. 

Recent detailed echocardiography identified a solitary functional ventricular chamber. The great arteries display a d-loop transposition, with the aorta arising anteriorly and rightward. Furthermore, there is complete imperforation of the pulmonary valve with an absence of forward flow. Reassuringly, the mitral valve is fully patent with preserved leaflet excursion, showing no evidence of atresia. Subsequent abdominal ultrasound demonstrated multiple small splenules distributed within the upper abdomen; splenic tissue was readily observed, confirming there is no splenic agenesis. Renal imaging and routine newborn blood screening tests were entirely normal.

Given these complex anatomical findings, I would value your clinical assessment and recommendations regarding the next steps in his care.

Sincerely,
Dr. Evelyn Vance
Pediatric Care Associates
